descriptionChirho: Persian loanword denoting the choice food or delicacy provided from the king's table, used exclusively in Daniel for the provisions offered to the captive youths. All multilingual glosses converge: Arabic طَعَام (food), Spanish comida/manjar (meal/delicacy), Korean 진미/음식 (delicacy/food), Hindi भोजन/रोटी (meal/bread), Swahili chakula (food). The four clusters differ only in prepositional framing (with, from, of) and pronominal suffixes (his, their), not in semantic content.
